title: Barcelona and Bilbao Tram Boycotts Turn into General Strike
reason: Confirmed: March 1951, Barcelona tram boycott spread to Bilbao, ~300,000 workers struck, first major protest since Civil War.

title: Pact of Madrid: US Military Bases End Spain's Cold War Isolation
reason: Event says 'four strategic bases' — actual agreement established five major bases (four air bases + one naval base at Rota). Materially wrong fact.

title: Concordat with the Holy See Cements Church-State Alliance
reason: Confirmed: signed 27 August 1953 between Spain and Vatican.

title: Spain Admitted to the United Nations
reason: Confirmed: admitted 14 December 1955 in package deal of 16 countries.

title: ETA Founded as Basque Separatist Organisation
reason: Confirmed: ETA founded 31 July 1959.

title: Stabilisation Plan Ends Autarky and Opens Spanish Economy
reason: Confirmed: approved July 1959, drafted with IMF/OECD assistance, devalued peseta.

title: Tourism Boom Transforms Spain into a Major Economic Power
reason: Event states 'over two million tourists visited in 1960' — actual figure was ~4.3 million in 1960 (Spain had already passed 2 million in 1958). Materially wrong fact.

title: EEC Rejects Spain's Membership Application on Democratic Grounds
reason: Confirmed: application submitted February 1962, rejected on democratic grounds; Munich Congress of European Movement June 1962.

title: Fraga Press Law Replaces Pre-Publication Censorship
reason: Confirmed: 1966 Press and Print Law promoted by Information Minister Manuel Fraga Iribarne.

title: ETA Carries Out First Killing, Escalating Basque Conflict
reason: Confirmed: June 7 1968, Txabi Etxebarrieta shot Civil Guard officer José Pardines Arcay; Etxebarrieta killed shortly after.

title: Franco Designates Juan Carlos as Monarchical Successor
reason: Confirmed: July 22 1969, Franco formally designated Juan Carlos as successor, bypassing Don Juan.

title: Burgos Military Trial of ETA Members Sparks International Protests
reason: Confirmed: December 1970, 16 ETA members tried, six death sentences, commuted by Franco on 30 December due to international pressure.

title: ETA Assassinates Prime Minister Carrero Blanco
reason: Confirmed: 20 December 1973, car bomb under Carrero Blanco's vehicle in central Madrid.

title: Arab Oil Embargo Ends Spain's Economic Miracle Decade
reason: Confirmed: October 1973 oil embargo hit Spain severely due to dependence on imported petroleum.

title: Franco Executes Five Political Prisoners Despite International Appeals
reason: Confirmed: 27 September 1975, two ETA and three FRAP members executed despite widespread international protests.

title: Franco Dies, Ending 36 Years of Dictatorship
reason: Confirmed: died 20 November 1975 from heart failure.

title: Juan Carlos I Proclaimed King of Spain
reason: Confirmed: proclaimed King on 22 November 1975, two days after Franco's death.

title: Law for Political Reform Dismantles Francoist Cortes
reason: Confirmed: passed by Cortes November 1976; December 1976 referendum approved with 94% yes on 77.7% turnout.

title: Atocha Massacre: Far-Right Gunmen Kill Labour Lawyers
reason: Confirmed: 24 January 1977, five PCE-linked labour lawyers killed; PCE's disciplined response accelerated its legalisation.

title: Communist Party Legalised, Completing Democratic Opening
reason: Confirmed: PCE legalised 9 April 1977 (Easter Saturday) by Suárez.

title: First Democratic Elections Since 1936
reason: Confirmed: 15 June 1977; UCD 34.4%, PSOE 29.3%.

title: Moncloa Pacts: Cross-Party Economic and Political Stabilisation
reason: Confirmed: signed 25 October 1977, nine major parties, wage restraint plus civil liberties commitments.

title: Democratic Constitution Ratified by Referendum
reason: Event states '88 percent in favour' — actual result was ~92% yes (91.81%) on 67–68% turnout. Materially wrong percentage.

title: Basque and Catalan Autonomy Statutes Approved
reason: Confirmed: both statutes sanctioned by Spanish Parliament 18 December 1979.

title: ETA's Deadliest Year: 60 People Killed
reason: 1980 was ETA's deadliest year (at least 92 killed), not 1979. The claim that 1979 was the deadliest year is materially wrong.

title: 23-F Military Coup Attempt Fails After King's TV Address
reason: Confirmed: 23 February 1981, Tejero stormed Congress; King's TV address in military uniform in early hours of 24 February collapsed the coup.

title: Spain Joins NATO Under Calvo-Sotelo Government
reason: Spain formally acceded to NATO on 30 May 1982, not 1981. Parliament voted October 1981, but the year of joining stated in the event is off by one year — the event places the accession in 1981.

title: PSOE Wins Historic Landslide: Felipe González Becomes PM
reason: Confirmed: 28 October 1982, PSOE won 202 seats (48% of vote), largest majority in Spanish democratic history.

title: Industrial Reconversion Closes Loss-Making State Enterprises
reason: Confirmed: González government's 1984 industrial reconversion restructured steel, shipbuilding; caused massive redundancies and union rift.

title: Spain Signs EEC Accession Treaty
reason: Confirmed: Treaty signed 12 June 1985 in Madrid; membership effective 1 January 1986.

title: NATO Referendum: Spain Votes to Remain in Alliance
reason: Event states 'yes vote won with 52 percent' — actual result was 56.9% yes. Materially wrong percentage.

title: ETA's Hipercor Supermarket Bombing Kills 21 Civilians
reason: Confirmed: 19 June 1987, 21 killed, 45 wounded; deadliest ETA attack.

title: General Strike Against PSOE Economic Policy Draws 8 Million Workers
reason: Confirmed: 14 December 1988, 8+ million workers, CCOO and UGT, country paralysed for 24 hours.

title: Barcelona Olympics and Seville Expo: Spain's Year of Prestige
reason: Confirmed: 1992 Barcelona Summer Olympics and Seville World Expo, coinciding with 500th anniversary of Columbus's voyage.

title: Peseta Devalued Three Times as EMS Crisis Triggers Recession
reason: Confirmed: three devaluations Sept 1992–May 1993; unemployment reached ~24–25% in 1993.

title: GAL State Terrorism Scandal Implicates Senior Government Officials
reason: Confirmed: GAL killed 27 ETA suspects; Garzón's investigation in 1994 led to Barrionuevo/Vera convictions. Event says 28 killed — minor discrepancy vs 27, otherwise accurate.

title: PP Wins Narrow Majority: Aznar Becomes Prime Minister
reason: Confirmed: March 1996, PP 38.85%, minority government with Catalan nationalist support.

title: ETA Murders Councillor Miguel Ángel Blanco, Triggering Mass Uprising
reason: Confirmed: kidnapped 10 July, shot 12 July 1997; millions took to streets across Spain.

title: Spain Locks Peseta to Euro, Entering Monetary Union
reason: Confirmed: EU Council assessed Spain as meeting EMU criteria in May 1998; exchange rate irrevocably fixed at 166.386 pesetas/euro from 1 January 1999.

title: PP Wins Absolute Majority: Aznar's Second Term
reason: Confirmed: March 2000, PP won 183 seats with 44.5% of vote.

title: Spain Joins Iraq War Coalition Against Massive Public Opposition
reason: Confirmed: Aznar joined US/UK at Azores summit March 2003 without UN mandate, opposed by ~90% of Spanish public.

title: Madrid Train Bombings Kill 191 People Three Days Before Election
reason: Confirmed: 11 March 2004, 10 bombs on 4 trains. Death toll debated between 191 and 193; event's '191' is within accepted range.

title: PSOE Wins Unexpected Election: Zapatero Withdraws Troops from Iraq
reason: Confirmed: 14 March 2004, PSOE won 164 seats, troops withdrawn by late May 2004.

title: Same-Sex Marriage Legalised Despite Church and Opposition Resistance
reason: Confirmed: third country in world; final parliamentary approval 30 June 2005, law effective 3 July 2005. Event says 'June 2005' for the approval — accurate.

title: Historical Memory Law Confronts Franco's Legacy
reason: Confirmed: enacted October 2007, condemned Franco dictatorship, required removal of Francoist symbols.

title: Spanish Housing Bubble Reaches Its Peak
reason: Confirmed: property market peaked 2007, construction ~16% of GDP, prices up ~200% since 1997.

title: Global Financial Crisis and Property Bust Devastate Spanish Economy
reason: Confirmed: double shock of global financial crisis and property bust; unemployment began rise toward 27%; cajas exposed.

title: Constitutional Tribunal Curbs Catalan Statute, Sparking Independence Movement
reason: Confirmed: ruling issued 28 June 2010, struck 14 articles, declared 'nation' reference legally void; 1.1–1.5 million marched.

title: Zapatero's Austerity U-Turn Under Financial Market Pressure
reason: Confirmed: May 2010 €15 billion austerity package; September 2010 general strike.

title: Indignados 15-M Movement Occupies City Squares Across Spain
reason: Confirmed: 15 May 2011, occupation of Puerta del Sol and squares across Spain; seeded Podemos.

title: ETA Announces Permanent Cessation of Armed Activity
reason: Confirmed: announced 20–21 October 2011 via video, following Aiete peace conference.

title: PP Wins Landslide Majority: Rajoy Replaces Zapatero
reason: Confirmed: November 2011, PP won 186 seats.

title: Spain Requests €100 Billion Banking Sector Bailout
reason: Confirmed: June 2012 request for up to €100 billion ESM credit line for bank recapitalisation; Bankia required €22.4 billion.

title: Unemployment Peaks at 27 Percent with Youth Rate Above 57 Percent
reason: Confirmed: Q1 2013, overall unemployment 26.9%, youth unemployment 56.9% (event says 'above 57%' — effectively correct).

title: King Juan Carlos Abdicates in Favour of Felipe VI
reason: Confirmed: abdication announced 2 June 2014, effective 19 June 2014; Felipe VI proclaimed King same day.

title: Podemos Founded, Disrupting Spain's Two-Party System
reason: Confirmed: founded January 2014 by Pablo Iglesias; won 5 EP seats in debut European election.

title: Fragmented Elections End PP-PSOE Duopoly
reason: Confirmed: December 2015, Podemos 69 seats, Ciudadanos 40 seats; no coalition formed, second election June 2016.

title: Catalonia's Illegal Independence Referendum and Article 155
reason: Confirmed: 1 October 2017 referendum; 27 October UDI declared; Senate invoked Article 155 same day.

title: Barcelona La Rambla Attack Kills 13 in Spain's Worst Jihadist Strike
reason: Confirmed: 17 August 2017, 13 killed initially (one more died 10 days later for total 14); Cambrils second attack hours later.

title: Rajoy Ousted in First Successful No-Confidence Vote in Spanish Democracy
reason: Confirmed: 1 June 2018, motion passed 180–169, first successful no-confidence vote; triggered by Gürtel corruption ruling.

title: Supreme Court Sentences Catalan Independence Leaders to Prison
reason: Confirmed: 14 October 2019, nine sentenced 9–13 years; Junqueras received 13 years.

title: Vox Far-Right Party Enters Parliament, Ending Spain's Exceptionalism
reason: Confirmed: April 2019 (24 seats), November 2019 (52 seats); ended Spain's resistance to far-right parliamentary representation.

title: COVID-19 State of Emergency: Spain Among Europe's Hardest Hit
reason: Confirmed: state of emergency 14 March 2020; ~28,000 deaths first wave; GDP contracted 10.8% in 2020.

title: Sánchez Forms First Coalition Government, Championing EU Recovery Fund
reason: Confirmed: PSOE-Unidas Podemos coalition formed January 2020; EU's €750 billion Next Generation fund negotiated July 2020, Spain allocated ~€140 billion.

title: Catalan Independence Leaders Pardoned in Reconciliation Gesture
reason: Confirmed: nine leaders pardoned June 2021 by Sánchez government; prison sentences commuted, civil disqualifications maintained.

title: Ukraine War Energy Crisis Drives Inflation to 40-Year High
reason: Confirmed: inflation peaked over 10% in 2022; Spain secured EU 'Iberian exception' gas price cap.

title: Inconclusive Elections and Catalan Amnesty Law Controversy
reason: Confirmed: July 2023 hung parliament; Feijóo failed to form government; Sánchez formed coalition with amnesty law as condition for Junts support.

title: Valencia Floods Kill Over 220 in Spain's Worst Natural Disaster
reason: Confirmed: 29 October 2024 flash floods, death toll 220–237 depending on source; event's 'over 220' is accurate.

title: Catalan Amnesty Law Enters Force Amid Ongoing Legal Challenges
reason: Confirmed: Constitutional Court upheld law as constitutional June 2025; Puigdemont separately excluded by Supreme Court; ECJ referrals pending.
